viz.priority: Interactive rendering is driven almost entirely by the GPU choice. Enscape, Lumion, D5, and TwinMotion scale directly with GPU power and VRAM. The RTX 5070 Ti hits the practical sweet spot for most architecture viz but the sky is the limit and more GPU power means faster rendering and more complex scenes are supported.

production.priority: V-Ray CPU and Corona are multi-thread CPU bound, with GPU hybrid modes available. Core count drives render times - AMD Ryzen 9 leads, and Threadripper PRO pulls further ahead if you're only rendering on that computer. GPU rendering continues to advance and it may be worth investigating switching away from CPU rendering.

PrebuiltTypeNotes.mini: Silent, tiny, no discrete GPU. Drives 2-4 monitors on integrated graphics. Perfect for document review, drafting, and light modeling.
PrebuiltTypeNotes.office: Standard office tower. Some accept a low-power GPU (RTX 4060 class, 115W). Good for drafting and modeling. Cannot fit a high-end GPU.
PrebuiltTypeNotes.workstation: ISV-certified, vPro, ECC optional. Real support. RTX Pro (not GeForce) GPUs -- fine for modeling, underpowered for serious viz.
PrebuiltTypeNotes.gaming: When you need a real GPU, buy a gaming desktop. 850W PSU, triple-slot GPU clearance, proper cooling. Outperforms a $4,000 workstation for Enscape/Lumion/V-Ray at half the price.
